theme.cycle_view: AI capex has not been cut and the demand prints are still accelerating: NVDA FQ3 FY27 revenue $115.8B +103% y/y with FQ4 guided ~$130B (2026-11-17), TSMC October revenue +59.7% y/y (2026-11-10), Arista guiding 2027 +38-40% (2026-11-03), Alphabet saying 2027 capex will 'increase significantly' and Microsoft trimming CY2026 capex only from $175B to ~$170B on supplier delays (2026-10-28/29). What changed since late October is the price and availability of capital, not demand: Alphabet's FCF went negative and the stock had its worst day ever (-12 to -13%, 2026-10-29), Amazon's TTM FCF is -$42.4B, Meta is raising up to ~$95B of equity, CoreWeave CDS trade at 1,100-1,290bp with its 2031 bond near 16%, OpenAI's round reportedly reached ~$11B of a $30B target, the 10Y is ~5% with a December Fed hike priced (late-October data; current level not found), Democrats won both chambers on 2026-11-03, and Jensen Huang resigned on 2026-11-12 amid board and FBI investigations. So this is a funding and de-rating shock on top of intact earnings: 2026 spend is safe, but 2027 growth now depends on capital markets reopening, and the layers that need outside money (neoclouds, power, quantum) are impaired while cash-generative chokepoints are being sold with them.
layer_ranking: 1. Compute & semis - earnings and guidance still rising, supply-constrained (TSM, ASML, HBM), largest de-rating; disagree with z_ai_theme, which ranks it low purely on trailing price. Prefer foundry/equipment over merchant GPU.

2. AI applications & data - split layer: security and infrastructure software have a confirmed demand read (PANW 2026-11-18, NET +39%) and need no capex funding; seat-based application software is where agents compress revenue (TEAM). Agree with the quant score for the first half only.

3. Cloud & frontier models - demand is strongest here (Azure +48%, AWS +39%) but this is where FCF is going negative and equity is being issued. z_ai_theme ranks it top on price; I agree only for AAPL and MSFT, not META/AMZN.

4. Datacenter, neocloud & power gear - ANET is the exception; the rest is levered, customer-concentrated and facing a credit market Evercore describes as 'no mas' to AI debt without operating cash flow. Agree with the low quant score.
5. AI power & materials - announcements ahead of revenue, long time to cash, funding-dependent; -32% 1m. Agree with quant.
6. Physical AI / frontier compute (robotics, self-driving, quantum) - cash burn with a higher cost of capital and a closed equity window. Agree with quant.
theme.z_ai_theme_comment: z_ai_theme is trailing price strength, so right now it is a measure of who has been sold least. It is right about the bottom three layers and wrong to put semis below hyperscalers on a 3-12 month view. All of this is a fundamental ranking; timing and gross exposure are the regime's call (RISK-OFF, VIX 36.9, 12% breadth).
theme.what_would_change_the_view: Downgrade to underweight if a big-four hyperscaler guides 2027 capex flat or down, if a large AI lab renegotiates compute contracts, or if the NVDA investigation leads to new China export restrictions. Upgrade if AI credit spreads tighten and AVGO (2026-12-09) and the January hyperscaler prints hold 2027 plans.

views.thesis: AI revenue is in the line: marketing-data platform, Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-09) revenue $493M +46% y/y, adj EPS $0.38 vs $0.28 consensus, FY2026 guidance raised on revenue, EBITDA, FCF and GAAP EPS. Not funded by hyperscaler capex; P/S 4.3 and FCF yield 3.2% (candidates file) are modest for the growth. Still 26% above MA200.
views.risks: Growth partly acquired (organic rate not verified here); thin GAAP margin (5.1% operating, candidates file); ad budgets are cyclical if the selloff hits the real economy; -11% 1m and below MA50.
views.next_earnings: unknown (next report expected ~Feb 2027, date not found)

views.thesis: Identity for AI agents is a real demand line and security is the one software group with a confirmed demand read (PANW 2026-11-18). But consensus for the October quarter is only ~10% growth to $816M, against P/S 10.9 (candidates file) and a stock one source puts up ~140% YTD. Fairly priced into a binary print.
views.risks: Earnings in about 7 trading days; valuation vs 10% growth; a miss in this tape gets punished hard (see TEAM).
views.next_earnings: 2026-12-01 (reported by secondary sources, not company-confirmed)

views.thesis: The capex-light hyperscaler: no AI build-out to fund, so the price-of-capital shock that is hitting the group does not touch it. FQ4 2026 (reported 2026-11-02) revenue $114.5B +12% vs 9-11% guidance, iPhone $57.6B +17.5%, December quarter guided to be the best revenue quarter in company history with iPhone Duo (on sale 2026-10-23) all incremental. Only AI-chain candidate above both MA50 and MA200.
views.risks: Management flagged memory-cost pressure on margins and supply constraints; earnings yield 2.65% / P/S 10.4 (candidates file) is not cheap; AI exposure is as a consumer of others' models, not a seller - this is a quality/defensive view, not an AI-growth view.
views.next_earnings: unknown (late Jan 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Data security/backup with 38% revenue growth (candidates file, quarter to 2026-07-31) and tailwind from the same security demand PANW confirmed. No fresh company data found for this run; operating margin -18% and P/S 14.3 make it a long-duration name in a rising cost-of-capital regime.
views.risks: Unprofitable on GAAP; FQ3 report due early December (date not found); -11% 1m.
views.next_earnings: not found (expected early Dec 2026)

views.thesis: Platform security leader and AI-agent security beneficiary; consensus for the October quarter is +23% to $1.53B. Group demand read is positive (PANW 2026-11-18, CRWD ~+6% premarket 2026-11-19). But P/S 43 (candidates file) and a forward P/E one source puts at 186x leave no margin for error at VIX ~37.
views.risks: Valuation; earnings in about 7 trading days; a technology-outage scare hit application software on 2026-11-17.
views.next_earnings: 2026-12-01 (reported by secondary sources, not company-confirmed)

views.thesis: Best-funded AI franchise with AI revenue visible: FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-10-28) Azure +48% to $33.2B, quarterly capex $45.2B but FCF still +$18.6B. CY2026 capex trimmed to ~$170B from $175B because third-party capacity slipped, not because demand fell; FY27 capex still guided up. Earnings yield 4.0%, operating margin 47% (candidates file). Self-funded, so it gains share if neoclouds cannot finance.
views.risks: FCF down 27% y/y; exposure to OpenAI, whose funding round reportedly closed ~$11B against a $30B target (WSJ via secondary sources, early Nov 2026); below MA50; next catalyst not until late January.
views.next_earnings: unknown (late Jan 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Core ads business is strong (revenue +26% y/y, operating margin 33%, earnings yield 5.3% - candidates file) and the stock is the cheapest hyperscaler. But it is funding AI capex ($135-145B for 2026, Q3 capex $34.9B) with an equity raise of up to ~$95B announced 2026-10-26, including new non-voting Class C shares - the clearest case in the group of capex outrunning internal cash flow, with no external cloud revenue to monetise it. Fell 7% the day after results (2026-10-22).
views.risks: Dilution and governance (non-voting class); no 2027 capex guide found; 17% below MA50 and below MA200 - one bad month from the knife filter.
views.next_earnings: unknown (late Jan 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Freshest positive print in scope: FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-11-18) revenue $3.45B +39% y/y, FY27 revenue guidance raised to $14.52-14.57B from $14.10-14.20B; lifted the whole security group on 2026-11-19. Security spend is not funded by the AI capex cycle and rises with AI adoption. Event risk is now behind it.
views.risks: Headline growth includes acquired revenue (organic split not verified); P/S 24 (candidates file); below MA50.
views.next_earnings: unknown (Feb 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Fundamentals are accelerating: Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-05) revenue $782.5M +39% y/y, non-GAAP operating income $137.1M (17.5% margin), GAAP operating loss $67.9M. Edge inference/agent traffic is a real usage line. Held at 0 on price: P/S 36 and FCF yield 0.3% (candidates file) make it the longest-duration name here in a price-of-capital shock.
views.risks: Valuation compression if 10Y stays ~5%; -24% off high and 14% below MA50.
views.next_earnings: unknown (early Feb 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Cheap on FCF (6.7% yield, P/S 4.2 - candidates file) with 13% growth, but it is seat-based HR/finance software, the category most exposed to agent-driven seat compression, and it reports in two sessions. No edge on the print.
views.risks: Binary earnings on 2026-11-24 in a tape that took TEAM down ~17-20% on a guidance trim; -16% 1m.

views.thesis: Reported numbers are strong: Q3 2026 (2026-11-03) revenue $13.38B +45%, data center $8.5B +97% on EPYC and the MI450 GPU launch, Q4 guided ~$17B (+~66% y/y) at ~55% gross margin. Held at 0 because the MI450 ramp leans on a small number of AI-lab/hyperscale buyers at the moment lab funding is tightening, inventory rose 35% q/q, and at P/S 15.3 / earnings yield 1.1% (candidates file) it is the most expensive semi in scope. Fell 6.3% on 2026-11-20.
views.risks: Customer concentration and vendor-supported demand in the GPU ramp (structure not re-verified this run); inventory build; 23% below MA50, 34% off high.
views.next_earnings: unknown (early Feb 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: Search/observability with a vector-search AI angle; cheap at P/S 4.3 and 4.5% FCF yield (candidates file); FQ1 FY27 cRPO $1.153B +21%. FQ2 (quarter ended 2026-10-31) results are due around now and I could not find them, so no view on the print. -24% 1m.
views.risks: Results imminent/not found; 15% growth is the slowest of the infrastructure-software names; consumption exposure.

Sells to the self-funded hyperscalers, not to levered neoclouds.

views.next_earnings: unknown (mid Feb 2027 expected, date not found)

views.thesis: The chokepoint with monthly hard data: October 2026 revenue NT$586.89B, +59.7% y/y and +14.7% m/m, a record and above the NT$560-570B analysts expected (reported 2026-11-10); Q4 guide US$52.3-54.3B. Orders are multi-year and placed by TSMC/memory makers, one step removed from AI-lab funding. -36% off high.

FQ1 FY27 (reported 2026-11-05) beat, but a forecast for slower subscription/cloud growth took the stock down ~17-20% and it is -39% over 1m (candidates file); fell another 6% on 2026-11-17. Developer-seat software is where coding agents bite first. It only escaped the knife filter because it is still above MA200.

views.next_earnings: unknown (late Jan/early Feb 2027 expected, date not found)

China/export-control exposure rises with the new Congress.

add_back.reason: Excluded as a falling knife, ~42% below its June record close, but the earnings driver is contracted: Micron said it raised HBM prices significantly for CY2027 with most 2027 HBM supply covered above 2026 prices, and NVDA lifted supply commitments to $390B, mostly memory (2026-11-19). The mid-November drop was a NAND price forecast, and NAND is ~a quarter of the business. Small, staged position only; memory is the most cyclical part of the chain.

Not excluded, ranked just below the cut (next_ranked). The -12 to -13% on 2026-10-29 was about negative FCF (-$5.9B reported by one source) and an EPS miss ($2.67 vs $3.02), not demand; it has its own silicon and a cloud business large enough to monetise the capex. Lower conviction than MU: 2027 EPS estimates are being cut and FCF is the issue the market is punishing.

Only if it is in the universe (not in candidates, next_ranked or the excluded list). FQ4 guided $34.8B (+93% y/y) with AI chips $21.7B, FY2027 AI semiconductor revenue projected at $115B, RPO $179.2B; reports 2026-12-09. Caveat: the RPO is attributed mainly to one custom-accelerator contract, so AI-lab funding risk applies. Wait for the print.

not_added_back.reason: Best fundamentals in the chain, but the screen is right for now: CEO resigned 2026-11-12, board and FBI investigations are open, interim CEO, and the outcome could tighten China export rules. Unquantifiable governance risk; revisit when the investigation scope is known.
